strengths: First real-world aerial 3D semantic scene completion benchmark, addressing a clear gap in the literature for UAV/drone-based 3D perception research
Practical image-based data generation framework that minimizes manual annotation by leveraging 2D-to-3D projection, avoiding expensive LiDAR hardware requirements
Comprehensive scale and diversity: 20,000+ samples across multiple altitudes (30m, 40m, 50m), seasons, and diverse environments (urban, industrial, rural) with high-resolution input imagery
High geometric fidelity demonstrated by 1.24 pixel average reprojection error and strong 3D reconstruction quality with >90% image overlap across scenes
Well-designed multi-dimensional evaluation framework including class-wise, group-wise, and altitude-wise analysis, supplemented by metric depth estimation benchmarking
Excellent reproducibility: detailed implementation documentation, supplementary material with semantic class distributions and per-scene statistics, and promised code/data release
Addresses practical needs for autonomous systems and robotics requiring holistic 3D scene understanding from aerial perspectives without LiDAR
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty—data generation pipeline relies entirely on established techniques (SfM, Poisson reconstruction, silhouette carving) with minimal novel algorithmic contributions specific to aerial 3D understanding

Insufficient baseline evaluation: only CCGFormer is benchmarked without comparisons to other recent SSC methods, ablations on pipeline design choices, or evidence the dataset reveals unique aerial-specific challenges

Ground-truth quality not independently validated—multi-stage pipeline (SfM→reconstruction→annotation→voxelization) introduces potential error accumulation; reprojection error alone does not ensure semantic accuracy; inter-annotator agreement and annotation guidelines not documented
Severe class imbalance (Building 75.7%, Flying Animal 0.001%) inadequately addressed with no documented strategies for balanced training/evaluation or analysis of impact on rare-class performance
Geographic scope extremely limited to 9 scenes in a single region, raising critical generalization concerns—unclear whether models will transfer to different regions, climates, or urban layouts

Overstated annotation efficiency: requires manual 2D semantic segmentation for ~10% of images per scene; the 2D-to-3D lifting depends on reconstruction quality and becomes a bottleneck for dataset extension

Depth estimation results (Table 4) show significant altitude-dependent performance degradation and dramatic improvement with in-domain fine-tuning, suggesting potential metric inconsistencies or domain gaps that are not thoroughly explained

Limited analysis of aerial-specific challenges and failure modes: no systematic study of how aerial perspective differs from ground-based SSC (different occlusion patterns, atmospheric effects, scale variations), no error analysis, and no justification of design choices (scene selection, altitude values, class taxonomy)
Missing ablations on data generation pipeline (voxel size, reconstruction parameters, densification strategies) and no analysis of how design choices impact final semantic quality
Minimal discussion articulating what specific research gaps OccuFly uniquely addresses beyond being the 'first aerial SSC dataset'

strengths: First real-world aerial SSC benchmark addressing a significant gap for autonomous aerial vehicles, with no direct competitors in the aerial domain
Large-scale, well-curated dataset: 20,000+ samples across 9 diverse scenes with multi-seasonal coverage and three environmental types (urban, industrial, rural)
Practical image-based data generation framework that leverages photogrammetry to automate ground-truth creation with <10% manual annotation, avoiding LiDAR sparsity limitations
Comprehensive and rigorous evaluation: benchmark suite covers multiple methods, altitude-wise metrics, class-wise analysis, and qualitative assessments revealing domain-specific challenges
High geometric fidelity demonstrated by 92% pixel-wise agreement in 3D reconstruction and 1.24-pixel average reprojection error
Thorough technical soundness: well-formulated problem statement, careful class-aware voxelization methodology, proper handling of surface/occluded/invalid voxel classes
Excellent reproducibility: detailed implementation specifications, dataset statistics, clear procedural documentation, and extensive visualization of data quality across 21 semantic classes
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: relies on commercial SfM software (Metashape), uses standard majority voting for label transfer, and employs conventional voxelization procedures without algorithmic innovation
Manual annotation overhead remains significant (9.17% on average at ~29 minutes per image), limiting scalability to larger geographic regions and creating bottleneck in data expansion
Narrow geographic scope: all 9 scenes from single region (Ingolstadt, Germany); limited altitude range (predominantly 30-50m, max ~80m); lack of geographic diversity limits generalization claims
Circular evaluation dependency: metric depth maps are derived from the same photogrammetric reconstruction that serves as ground-truth, potentially inflating reported quality metrics

Incomplete analysis of key findings: altitude-induced performance degradation documented but not mechanistically analyzed; severe underperformance of modern methods (DepthAnything v2) lacks investigation

Missing ablation studies on data generation pipeline components; no systematic analysis of reconstruction failures in textureless or repetitive regions; reconstruction error propagation to downstream tasks not characterized

Evaluated methods are primarily terrestrial SSC models without aerial adaptation; no baseline methods specifically designed for aerial domain; limited insights into required architectural modifications for aerial transfer

Data generation framework dependencies not fully transparent: requires >90% image overlap (operationally impractical), relies on commercial software, and kNN refinement parameters (k=100, ε=20) lack justification
